andhraPradesh.headline: Cabinet approves Amaravati Sangamam and additional land pooling for capital infrastructure
facts: The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet approved administrative sanction of ₹759.793 crore, including applicable charges, for Amaravati Sangamam at Shakamuru.
The proposed complex comprises the Andhra Pradesh State Public Library, an auditorium and the Global Institute of Good Governance.
The Cabinet authorised pooling of 6,212.50 acres in Kantheru and Tadikonda mandal for capital-region infrastructure.
Reported land components are 974 acres in Kantheru and 5,238 acres in Tadikonda; the planned works include the Inner Ring Road, railway-line corridor and grid roads.
These are Cabinet approvals; the decision does not mean the works are completed or operational.
andhraPradesh.summary: At its 3 September meeting, the State Cabinet approved Amaravati Sangamam and another round of land pooling for planned capital infrastructure. The decisions concern administrative sanction and land pooling, not project completion.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Urban planning, land pooling and capital-region development
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Amaravati Sangamam is planned at Shakamuru and includes a public library, auditorium and governance institute; the land pooling covers Kantheru and Tadikonda.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Examine how capital-region infrastructure can be balanced with transparent land pooling, farmer participation, fiscal prudence and accountable project delivery.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Both the projects and the land pooling are located in Andhra Pradesh’s Amaravati capital region.

andhraPradesh.headline: Cabinet sanctions restructuring of 13,252 rural water-supply works under JJM 2.0
facts: The Cabinet approved revival, restructuring and administrative sanction for 13,252 rural water-supply works at an estimated ₹4,053.85 crore under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.
The plan rationalises 13,247 Single Village Scheme works into 7,439 schemes, estimated at ₹3,046.11 crore.
Five Multi-Village Schemes, estimated at ₹1,007.74 crore, are to cover 334 villages.

The Cabinet also approved an accountability framework including a two-year defect-liability period; multi-village and bulk-water schemes are to have an additional 10-year performance-based operation and maintenance period.
The decision is an approval for restructuring and completing works, not confirmation that all works have been completed.
andhraPradesh.summary: The Cabinet approved a ₹4,053.85-crore restructuring package for unfinished rural drinking-water works under JJM 2.0. The plan reorganises village schemes and sets out defect-liability and longer-term maintenance requirements.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Rural drinking-water governance and Jal Jeevan Mission
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The approved package covers 13,252 works; five multi-village schemes are planned to cover 334 villages.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how scheme rationalisation, water-quality monitoring and long-term operation and maintenance affect the sustainability of rural tap-water access.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The Cabinet decision applies to rural drinking-water infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh.

andhraPradesh.headline: A. Konduru drinking-water project completed, serving 38 habitations in NTR district
facts: The ₹49.94-crore Jal Jeevan Mission–Amarajeevi Jaladhara project in A. Konduru mandal, NTR district, was reported complete on 3 September.
The project draws Krishna water through the NTPC canal at Ibrahimpatnam, treats it and supplies it through a 130-km pipeline network.
The network includes 12 overhead tanks and is intended to serve about 75,000 people in 38 habitations across 21 gram panchayats.
The stated service level is 55 litres of potable water per person per day.
The 38 habitations include 15 tribal hamlets; the project addresses long-standing access to safe drinking water.
andhraPradesh.summary: The completed A. Konduru project brings treated Krishna water to households across 38 habitations in NTR district. Reports describe it as a 26-month project designed to serve around 75,000 people, including residents of 15 tribal hamlets.

andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: A. Konduru is in NTR district; the project uses a 130-km pipeline, 12 overhead tanks and a stated supply target of 55 litres per person daily.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Explain how safe-water infrastructure can advance preventive health and equity, while noting the need for continuous water-quality testing and reliable operation and maintenance.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The project is in A. Konduru mandal, NTR district, Andhra Pradesh.

andhraPradesh.headline: Forest Department directed to study wildlife deaths and conservation measures statewide
facts: On 3 September, Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister and Forest Minister K. Pawan Kalyan directed the Forest Department to undertake a comprehensive study of recent wildlife deaths and conservation measures.
The study is to examine habitat management, migration corridors, anti-poaching measures, monitoring, forest-fire control and water availability.
A high-level committee chaired by Forest Department Adviser P. Mallikarjuna Rao, with Additional Principal Chief Conservator of Forests Rahul Pandey as member-convener, was assigned the work.
The review is to cover conservation of tigers, leopards, elephants and other wildlife, and identify measures to reduce human-wildlife conflict.
The directive calls for assessment and recommendations; it is not a report of completed findings.
andhraPradesh.summary: The State directed a statewide assessment of wildlife deaths and the effectiveness of field-level conservation measures. The committee is to review habitat and corridor conditions, monitoring, water availability and conflict prevention before submitting recommendations.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Wildlife conservation, habitat corridors and the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The committee is chaired by Forest Department Adviser P. Mallikarjuna Rao; Rahul Pandey is its member-convener.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how evidence-led monitoring, habitat connectivity and coordination between forest-edge communities and agencies can reduce wildlife mortality and human-wildlife conflict.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The study covers wildlife habitats and conservation measures across Andhra Pradesh.

andhraPradesh.headline: State sanctions ₹9.94 crore for preparatory works for Guntur yoga and naturopathy institute
facts: The State government sanctioned ₹9.94 crore for preparatory works at the proposed Central Research Institute of Yoga and Naturopathy site at Nadimpalem, Prathipadu mandal, near Guntur.
The preparatory allocation comprises ₹6.74 crore for land-related requirements and ₹3.20 crore for site filling and levelling, according to the report.
The Union Ministry of AYUSH is to support the proposed institute through a ₹100-crore grant under the Central Council for Research in Yoga and Naturopathy.
The proposed facility includes a 100-bed hospital and research facilities on a site of about 15 acres.
The preparatory sanction advances site preparation; the institute is not yet operational.
andhraPradesh.summary: The State announced a ₹9.94-crore sanction for preparatory site works for the proposed Guntur institute, complementing the Centre’s stated ₹100-crore support. The project remains at the preparation stage, with construction and operations still ahead.

andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The proposed institute is at Nadimpalem in Prathipadu mandal near Guntur and is planned to include a 100-bed hospital.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess the potential of public investment in research-backed traditional medicine alongside the need for clinical evidence, qualified personnel and accessible care.

andhraPradesh.headline: Dentic World dental-technology hub inaugurated at AMTZ in Visakhapatnam

The hub brings dental-technology research, design, prototyping and advanced manufacturing under one platform.
AMTZ and Homi Bhabha Cancer Hospital & Research Centre signed an MoU for collaboration in radiopharmaceuticals, radiochemistry and oncology research.

national.headline: Government launches BIO-NIVESH platform to connect biotechnology innovators with investors
facts: BIO-NIVESH was launched on 3 September 2026 by the Union Ministry of Science & Technology.
The platform is intended to link biotechnology innovators and entrepreneurs with investors and industry.
Its objective is to catalyse private investment and help promising innovations scale up and reach commercial markets.
The government described BIO-NIVESH as a recurring platform, with future editions proposed in different cities.

national.headline: Defence Minister releases RAKSHA framework for India’s defence diplomacy
facts: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh released the RAKSHA document in New Delhi on 3 September 2026.
The document sets out a strategic roadmap for India’s global defence partnerships over the next 10 years.
Its stated pillars include strategic partnerships, capacity building, promotion of indigenous defence exports and maritime security.
The framework identifies India’s role as a net security provider and first responder in the Indian Ocean Region as a defence-diplomacy priority.
national.summary: The Ministry of Defence released RAKSHA as a decade-long framework for India’s defence diplomacy. It links national-security objectives with international partnerships, training and capacity building, indigenous defence exports and maritime security cooperation.

national.prelimsTakeaway: RAKSHA is the Ministry of Defence’s 10-year strategic roadmap for global defence partnerships.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how defence diplomacy can advance strategic partnerships, indigenous defence manufacturing and regional maritime security.

national.headline: India and Belgium outline expanded cooperation in trade, defence, renewable energy and technology
facts: The India–Belgium joint statement followed Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever’s official visit to India from 2–4 September 2026.
The leaders supported a goal of doubling bilateral trade over the following five years.
The statement welcomed a renewed India–Belgium memorandum of understanding on renewable-energy cooperation, including green hydrogen, solar, energy storage and offshore wind.
The leaders welcomed a defence cooperation letter of intent and a memorandum of understanding between India’s CBI and Belgium’s Federal Police.
Belgium supported India’s permanent membership of a reformed and expanded UN Security Council.
national.summary: India and Belgium used the Prime Minister’s visit to set out a broad cooperation agenda spanning trade, renewable energy, defence, technology and law enforcement. The joint statement also recorded Belgium’s support for India’s permanent membership of a reformed UN Security Council.

national.prelimsTakeaway: The statement covered a five-year bilateral trade-doubling goal, renewable-energy cooperation and defence and law-enforcement collaboration.
national.mainsAngle: Evaluate how bilateral partnerships can advance trade, clean-energy transition and India’s diplomatic objectives in multilateral institutions.

national.headline: CCI directs four entities to cease anti-competitive benchmark pricing in debenture trusteeship
facts: The Competition Commission of India issued its order on 2 September 2026; the order was publicised by PIB on 3 September.
The order names the Trustees’ Association of India, IDBI Trusteeship Services, Axis Trustee Services and SBI CAP Trustee Company, along with individuals liable under Section 48.
CCI found conduct involving benchmark-price fixing for debenture trusteeship services during FY 2020–21 and FY 2021–22.
The Commission found violations of Section 3(3)(a) and Section 3(3)(b), read with Section 3(1), of the Competition Act, 2002.
CCI directed the parties to cease and desist from the anti-competitive conduct under Section 27 of the Act.
national.summary: CCI ordered four trusteeship-sector entities and associated individuals to cease conduct it found anti-competitive in the provision of debenture trusteeship services. The order was dated 2 September 2026 and publicly reported the following day.
national.staticLink: Competition law, market conduct and regulatory enforcement
national.prelimsTakeaway: CCI cited Sections 3(1), 3(3)(a), 3(3)(b), 27 and 48 of the Competition Act, 2002, in the order.
national.mainsAngle: Examine the role of competition regulation in preventing coordinated price-setting and protecting fair market practices in financial services.

national.headline: Centre reviews Himalayan states’ preparedness for GLOFs and snow avalanches
facts: Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan chaired the preparedness review in New Delhi on 3 September 2026.
Participants included Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir, along with MHA, NDMA, CWC, IMD and DGRE officials.
The review focused on monitoring vulnerable glacial lakes and snow-covered areas, identifying high-risk locations and planning potential flow paths.
The meeting emphasised early warnings, last-mile alert dissemination, evacuation preparedness and coordinated response.
States were asked to expedite GLOF mitigation projects sanctioned by the Central Government in 2024.
national.summary: The Centre reviewed preparedness for glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) and snow avalanches with Himalayan states and disaster-management and technical agencies. The meeting stressed risk monitoring, early warning, evacuation readiness and faster implementation of previously sanctioned mitigation projects.
national.staticLink: Glacial hazards, early-warning systems and disaster-risk reduction
national.prelimsTakeaway: GLOF preparedness involves monitoring glacial lakes, forecasting and alert dissemination, flow-path planning, evacuation and inter-agency coordination.

national.headline: India records year-on-year growth in crude and finished steel production during April–August
facts: The Ministry of Steel released production and demand figures on 3 September 2026.
Crude steel production for April–August 2026 was 70.3 million tonnes, up 1.8% from 69.0 million tonnes a year earlier.
Finished steel production for April–August 2026 was 68.1 million tonnes, up 3.8% from 65.6 million tonnes.
Finished-steel consumption for April–August was 70.3 million tonnes, 7.0% above the corresponding period of the previous year.
India was a net importer of finished steel by quantity during April–August 2026.
national.summary: The Ministry of Steel’s update showed year-on-year increases in crude-steel and finished-steel production for April–August 2026, alongside faster growth in finished-steel consumption. India remained a net importer of finished steel by quantity over the period.

national.headline: Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari reports more than 1.58 crore groundwater-recharge structures
facts: Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari (JSJB) was launched on 6 September 2024 to promote community-led water conservation.
The initiative supports low-cost groundwater-recharge and water-storage structures and the revival of defunct borewells.
The government reported more than 1.58 crore artificial groundwater-recharge structures as of 3 September 2026.
In June 2026, JSJB was integrated with Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain as JSJB: Catch the Rain.

national.headline: Decentralised grain-storage plan completes godowns in 313 PACS
facts: The Decentralised Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector was launched in 2023 and works through Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS).
As of July 2026, godown construction was completed in 313 PACS, adding more than 1.80 lakh metric tonnes of storage capacity.
The plan aims to improve local storage, processing, procurement and distribution through a cooperative-led approach.
The National Cooperative Development Corporation is the plan’s implementing agency.
The plan seeks to bring storage closer to production centres, reduce transportation costs and limit foodgrain wastage.
national.summary: A PIB backgrounder reported that godowns had been completed in 313 PACS by July 2026, creating over 1.80 lakh metric tonnes of capacity. national.headline: NHAI announces Green Highways Excellence Awards 2026; Chilakaluripet Bypass wins in avenue-plantation category
facts: NHAI announced the 2026 Green Highways Excellence Award winners across avenue plantations, median plantations and plantation in land parcels.

national.headline: CSIR-CMERI inaugurates NAMASTE occupational-safety training for sewer and septic-tank workers
facts: CSIR-CMERI inaugurated a 30-hour occupational-safety upskilling programme for sewer and septic-tank workers at its Durgapur campus on 3 September 2026.

international.headline: WMO forecasts a very strong El Niño persisting through February 2027
facts: The World Meteorological Organization’s August 2026 El Niño/La Niña Update was released on 3 September 2026.
WMO forecast a near-100% likelihood that El Niño would persist through February 2027 and strengthen to very strong intensity before peaking toward the end of 2026.
The forecast warned of increased risks of shifts in rainfall and temperature patterns, including floods, drought and extreme heat; regional impacts vary.
WMO’s forecast draws on contributions from global centres and national meteorological services, including India’s IMD and IITM.
The forecast is a prediction, not an observation of future weather; WMO says locally relevant warnings come from national meteorological services.
international.summary: On 3 September, WMO published its August update forecasting a very strong El Niño, with near-100% likelihood of persistence through February 2027. The outlook raises preparedness concerns for climate-sensitive sectors, while WMO cautions that impacts differ by region.
international.staticLink: El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO), Indian Ocean Dipole, monsoon variability and disaster-risk reduction.
international.prelimsTakeaway: El Niño is the warm phase of ENSO, associated with warming of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific; distinguish WMO’s seasonal forecast from locally issued weather warnings.
international.mainsAngle: Assess how early-warning systems and coordination among meteorological services can reduce climate risks to agriculture, water, health and disaster management.

international.headline: WHO validates Timor-Leste’s elimination of trachoma as a public-health problem
facts: WHO validated Timor-Leste as having eliminated trachoma as a public-health problem on 3 September 2026.
Trachoma, caused by the bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis, is the world’s leading infectious cause of blindness.
Timor-Leste was the last country in WHO’s South-East Asia Region where endemic trachoma was suspected; WHO said the disease is now eliminated as a public-health problem throughout the region.

The validation followed evidence including a 2025 survey of 4,949 samples from children aged 1–5 years across all 13 Timor-Leste municipalities, which found no transmission requiring trachoma-specific public-health intervention.
WHO counted Timor-Leste as the fourth country in its South-East Asia Region and the 33rd worldwide to achieve this milestone; India is among the countries previously validated.
international.summary: WHO’s validation confirmed that trachoma is no longer a public-health problem anywhere in its South-East Asia Region. The milestone followed multi-year investigation and surveillance, with Timor-Leste the final country in the region where endemic disease was suspected.
international.staticLink: Neglected tropical diseases, WHO validation, disease surveillance and universal health coverage.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Trachoma is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis; WHO validation denotes elimination as a public-health problem, not the end of surveillance or treatment for individual cases.
international.mainsAngle: Use the regional milestone to discuss evidence-based disease elimination, integrated surveillance, primary eye care and the role of water, sanitation and hygiene.

international.headline: Pacific Islands Forum leaders record concern over China’s missile launch, without unanimity
facts: At the Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting in Palau, leaders agreed to record collective concern about China’s July 2026 ballistic-missile launch into the South Pacific.
The statement was not unanimous: Nauru dissented from the clause expressing concern, according to Associated Press reporting from the summit’s closing day.
The Forum’s end-of-summit communiqué is normally decided by unanimous consensus; Kiribati had no representative at the leaders’ retreat, AP reported.
The development highlights the challenge of maintaining regional consensus amid major-power competition in the Pacific.
international.summary: On the summit’s closing day, Pacific leaders agreed to a statement of concern about China’s missile launch, but the position was not unanimous. Nauru dissented, while Kiribati had no representative at the retreat where leaders discussed the communiqué.
international.staticLink: Regional organisations, consensus-based diplomacy, Indo-Pacific geopolitics and small-island states.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The Pacific Islands Forum is a regional forum whose leaders’ communiqué is normally settled by consensus; this statement of concern over the missile launch was not unanimous.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss how strategic competition can test regional consensus and the diplomatic agency of small-island states in the Indo-Pacific.
